title: Ecommerce Sellers Face New EU Product Identifier Requirements
summary: EU product identifier rules affect ecommerce sellers. Learn what customs needs and how accurate product data supports cross-border shipping.
body_markdown:
Ecommerce sellers shipping goods directly to EU consumers now need product identifiers in customs declarations. The[European Commission](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/news/product-identifiers-e-commerce-imports-mandatory-1-november-2026-2026-11-03_en) says the requirement supports more precise checks for unsafe or noncompliant products.


Declarations require a seller or marketplace product reference, a manufacturer’s model or part number, and a standardized identifier, such as a retail barcode, where one exists. If no standardized identifier exists, the declaration must include an exemption code. The identifiers distinguish specific products, while tariff codes describe the categories of goods crossing the border.


For ecommerce sellers, incomplete product records can affect delivery.[eBay’s seller guidance](https://pages.ebay.com/eu-product-identifiers/) notes that missing identifiers may cause customs clearance delays or delivery disruptions, making accurate listing and supplier data part of the shipping process.


Review your product catalog, request missing identifiers from suppliers, and confirm how your carrier or customs representative receives them. Check that each identifier matches the exact item sold.
